claims.title: Aja migrations from Tado
claims.summary: Aja-speaking peoples spread, by oral tradition, eastward from Tado on the Mono River across the coastal plain of southern Benin, founding a cluster of kin-based kingdoms including Allada.

sources.label: History of the Kingdom of Dahomey

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1100-aja-migrations-from-tado, claim TL:BEN:event:1100:aja-migrations-from-tado, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Kingdom of Allada
claims.summary: Allada (Great Ardra) emerged as the leading Aja kingdom of the coastal region and the dynastic source from which the kingdoms of Dahomey and Porto-Novo would branch.

sources.label: History of the Kingdom of Dahomey

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1500-rise-of-the-kingdom-of-allada, claim TL:BEN:event:1500:rise-of-the-kingdom-of-allada, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Porto-Novo
claims.summary: The prince Te-Agbanlin, of the Allada royal house, founded the lagoon settlement of Hogbonu (Ajashe), later named Porto-Novo, which grew into a coastal port-kingdom of mixed Aja and Yoruba population.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1600-founding-of-porto-novo, claim TL:BEN:event:1600:founding-of-porto-novo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Dahomey at Abomey
claims.summary: Fon rulers established the Kingdom of Dahomey on the Abomey plateau; King Houegbadja is credited with beginning the Royal Palaces of Abomey and building a strongly centralised monarchy.

sources.label: History of the Kingdom of Dahomey
Royal Palaces of Abomey — World Heritage List, no. 323

claims.title: Dahomey conquers Allada
claims.summary: King Agaja's army overran Allada, the parent kingdom of the Fon dynasty, beginning Dahomey's drive toward the coast and the Atlantic trade.

sources.label: History of the Kingdom of Dahomey

claims.title: Conquest of Ouidah (Whydah)
claims.summary: Agaja seized the major slaving port of Whydah (Ouidah), giving Dahomey direct control of one of the busiest points of embarkation on the Slave Coast.

sources.label: Ouidah: The Social History of a West African Slaving Port 1727–1892 (Robin Law)

claims.title: Tributary to the Oyo Empire
claims.summary: Dahomey's expansion brought it into conflict with the Yoruba empire of Oyo to the east, to which it became tributary for much of the eighteenth century.

sources.label: History of the Kingdom of Dahomey

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1730-tributary-to-the-oyo-empire, claim TL:BEN:event:1730:tributary-to-the-oyo-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Royal Palaces of Abomey
claims.summary: A line of kings built earthen palaces decorated with polychrome bas-reliefs within a single great enclosure at Abomey; the complex was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.

sources.label: Royal Palaces of Abomey — World Heritage List, no. 323
The Royal Palaces of Abomey: Palace of King Behanzin, Benin

claims.title: Ouidah and the Atlantic slave trade
claims.summary: The port of Ouidah served for nearly two centuries as a leading point of embarkation on the Slave Coast, through which more than a million enslaved Africans are estimated to have been deported across the Atlantic.

sources.label: Ouidah: The Social History of a West African Slaving Port 1727–1892 (Robin Law)
Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database (Bight of Benin / Ouidah)

claims.title: Ghezo seizes the throne
claims.summary: Ghezo overthrew his brother Adandozan with the support of the Brazilian slave trader Francisco Félix de Sousa, beginning a reign that would expand Dahomey's army and its female Agojie regiment.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1818-ghezo-seizes-the-throne, claim TL:BEN:event:1818:ghezo-seizes-the-throne, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dahomey breaks free of Oyo
claims.summary: Ghezo defeated the weakened Yoruba empire of Oyo, ending the tributary status Dahomey had borne since the early eighteenth century and asserting full independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1823-dahomey-breaks-free-of-oyo, claim TL:BEN:event:1823:dahomey-breaks-free-of-oyo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British blockade of Dahomey's ports
claims.summary: Britain imposed a naval blockade to force Dahomey to end the slave trade; Ghezo agreed in 1852 but soon resumed slaving, as palm oil rose to become the kingdom's chief legitimate export.

sources.label: The compatibility of the slave and palm oil trades in Dahomey, 1818–1858
sources.publisher: Cambridge University Press (From Slave Trade to 'Legitimate' Commerce)

claims.title: First written record of the women warriors
claims.summary: European observers recorded Dahomey's distinctive all-female troops — the Agojie or Mino, later called the 'Amazons' — who would become an elite, high-status corps of the royal army.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1729-first-written-record-of-the-women-warriors, claim TL:BEN:event:1729:first-written-record-of-the-women-warriors, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Franco-Dahomean War
claims.summary: King Behanzin's forces clashed with the French around Cotonou; though repelled by superior French weaponry, the war marked the opening of Dahomey's struggle against French expansion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1890-first-franco-dahomean-war, claim TL:BEN:event:1890:first-franco-dahomean-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French conquest of Dahomey
claims.summary: A French expedition under Colonel Alfred-Amédée Dodds advanced on Abomey; Behanzin burned the capital rather than surrender it, and after further resistance capitulated in January 1894.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1892-french-conquest-of-dahomey, claim TL:BEN:event:1892:french-conquest-of-dahomey, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Behanzin deposed and exiled
claims.summary: France deposed the last independent king of Dahomey and exiled him to Martinique and later Algeria, where he died in 1906; the kingdom passed under French control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1894-behanzin-deposed-and-exiled, claim TL:BEN:event:1894:behanzin-deposed-and-exiled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colony of French Dahomey
claims.summary: Dahomey was organised as a French colony with its capital at Porto-Novo and incorporated into the federation of French West Africa, where it remained for six decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1899-colony-of-french-dahomey, claim TL:BEN:event:1899:colony-of-french-dahomey, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence as the Republic of Dahomey
claims.summary: Dahomey became a fully independent state on 1 August 1960, with Hubert Maga as its first president, ending French colonial rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-as-the-republic-of-dahomey, claim TL:BEN:event:1960:independence-as-the-republic-of-dahomey, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The cycle of coups begins
claims.summary: General Christophe Soglo deposed President Hubert Maga in Dahomey's first military coup, opening more than a decade of chronic instability and repeated seizures of power.

sources.label: Benin — Decolonization, independence and military coups

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1963-the-cycle-of-coups-begins, claim TL:BEN:event:1963:the-cycle-of-coups-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kérékou seizes power
claims.summary: Major Mathieu Kérékou overthrew the Presidential Council in the last of Dahomey's coups, ending the era of regional deadlock and establishing a durable military government.

sources.label: Benin — Decolonization, independence and military coups

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1972-kerekou-seizes-power, claim TL:BEN:event:1972:kerekou-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Adoption of Marxism-Leninism
claims.summary: Kérékou proclaimed Marxism-Leninism as the official ideology of the state, nationalising key sectors and aligning the country with the Eastern bloc.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1974-adoption-of-marxism-leninism, claim TL:BEN:event:1974:adoption-of-marxism-leninism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dahomey renamed Benin
claims.summary: Kérékou renamed the country the People's Republic of Benin, after the Bight of Benin, formally retiring the name Dahomey inherited from the precolonial Fon kingdom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1975-dahomey-renamed-benin, claim TL:BEN:event:1975:dahomey-renamed-benin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Collapse of the Marxist state
claims.summary: Amid economic ruin, unpaid wages and mass protest, Kérékou renounced Marxism-Leninism, setting the stage for a negotiated transition to democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1989-collapse-of-the-marxist-state, claim TL:BEN:event:1989:collapse-of-the-marxist-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The National Conference
claims.summary: A sovereign National Conference of the nation's 'living forces' met in Cotonou, stripped Kérékou of power and launched a transitional government — a pioneering model of peaceful democratic transition for Africa.

sources.label: The national conference as a model for democratic transition: Benin and Nigeria

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1990-the-national-conference, claim TL:BEN:event:1990:the-national-conference, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Multiparty constitution adopted
claims.summary: Voters approved a new democratic constitution by referendum, establishing a multiparty presidential republic and ending the Marxist one-party state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1990-multiparty-constitution-adopted, claim TL:BEN:event:1990:multiparty-constitution-adopted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Soglo defeats Kérékou at the polls
claims.summary: Nicéphore Soglo won the presidential election, and Kérékou peacefully handed over power — a rare democratic alternation in the Africa of the time.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1991-soglo-defeats-kerekou-at-the-polls, claim TL:BEN:event:1991:soglo-defeats-kerekou-at-the-polls, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kérékou returns by election
claims.summary: Having peacefully left office, Mathieu Kérékou returned to the presidency by winning the 1996 election, serving until term limits obliged him to step down in 2006.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Benin: From the Aja kingdoms of Allada and Porto-Novo and the Fon Kingdom of Dahomey at Abomey, through conquest and the slave trade, to a pioneering African democracy.", terralore.co/country/BEN/chronicle#ev-1996-kerekou-returns-by-election, claim TL:BEN:event:1996:kerekou-returns-by-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France returns the Abomey treasures
claims.summary: France formally returned 26 royal artworks looted from the palaces of Abomey during the 1892 conquest, a landmark act of cultural restitution to be displayed in Benin.

sources.label: France formally returns looted Benin artworks at Élysée ceremony
129-Year Journey Nears End as France Returns Benin Treasures
